channel.title: Charter Ed Digest
channel.description: News, trends, and practical guidance for charter school leaders and families

item.title: How School Culture Shapes K-8 Student Outcomes
item.description: School culture is a hidden driver of K-8 academic success. Learn what a college-going culture looks like, what the research shows, and what families should look for.

item.title: ABA Therapy & Insurance: What Florida Autism Families Need to Know
item.description: Florida mandates ABA therapy coverage—but plan-type gaps, prior auth delays, and managed-care shifts still trip families up. Here's how to navigate it in 2026.

item.title: Dual Enrollment Boom: What Charter Schools Must Know
item.description: 3.1 million students took college courses in 2024-25. Here's how charter schools can lead on dual enrollment equity—and why it matters for families choosing a school.

item.title: Why Charter Schools Are Leading the Reading Revolution
item.description: 70% of 4th graders can't read proficiently. Here's why charter schools are built to fix that—and what families should ask about any school's reading program.

item.title: CTE Pathways in Charter Schools: The New Equity Frontier
item.description: How charter schools use structured CTE pathways and industry credentials to build career readiness and close opportunity gaps for underserved students.

item.title: Is Your Child's School Losing Teachers? What to Ask
item.description: 1 in 8 teaching positions is vacant or understaffed in 2026. Here's how families can evaluate school staffing stability before enrolling.

item.title: The 4-Day School Week Debate: What Families Should Know
item.description: The 4-day school week is spreading fast—but research shows real academic costs. Here's what K-12 families and charter leaders need to know in 2026.

item.title: Beyond Test Scores: SEL as a School Choice Factor in 2026
item.description: More families in 2026 are choosing charter and option schools based on SEL. Here's what social-emotional learning really means and how to evaluate it.

item.description: Charter schools must provide IEPs—just like district schools. Here's what families of students with disabilities gain by choosing a flex or independent-study charter in 2026.

item.title: Charter Schools Have No Attendance Zones. Here's What That Means.
item.description: Charter schools don't use attendance zones — but eligibility still has rules. Here's what "open to all" really means for families in 2026.

item.title: Virtual School Clubs: Why They Matter More Than You Think
item.description: Clubs and extracurriculars in virtual charter schools aren't extras—they're essential for belonging, motivation, and outcomes. Here's what families need to know.

item.title: Project-Based Learning: The Research Case in 2026
item.description: New 2026 research confirms PBL's strong effect on K-12 achievement. Here's what charter school leaders and families need to know about the evidence.

item.title: AI Literacy in Charter Schools: The 2026 Edge
item.description: AI literacy is reshaping K–12 graduation requirements in 2026. Here's how charter schools are uniquely positioned to lead—and what families should look for.

item.title: Charter Schools as Family Launchpads in 2026
item.description: In 2026, the strongest charter schools go beyond academics—connecting families to healthcare, wealth-building accounts, and cradle-to-career pipelines that drive real economic mobility.

item.description: ESA programs are reshaping school choice in 2026. New AEI research shows what charter leaders must do to stay competitive—and what families should ask before choosing.

item.description: A practical guide to the charter school enrollment and lottery process — timelines, priority rules, waitlist tips, and common mistakes to avoid.

item.description: Charter schools have a structural edge in Science of Reading adoption. Here's why that matters—and how leaders can capitalize on it in 2026-27.

item.description: What should families ask about AI in 2026 school tours? Here's why AI literacy now belongs at the top of every parent's school-choice checklist.
